question: Why do nurses change a patient's body position in bed?

options.A: To make the bed look neat and tidy
options.B: To prepare the room for the doctor's visit
options.C: To help the body work well and prevent injuries
options.D: To help the patient sleep for more hours

explanation: Spot on! Proper positioning keeps the body's systems functioning smoothly and protects the skin from pressure sores. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why is knowing how to position patients a key skill for student nurses?

options.A: It directly affects skin comfort, safety, and breathing
options.B: It is the only duty a student is allowed to do
options.C: It replaces the need to give medications
options.D: It stops all risks of being in the hospital

explanation: You got it! Positioning touches almost every part of patient care, making it a vital skill to master for safe practice. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: When moving a patient in bed, why should you lift them rather than drag them?

options.A: To prevent sudden drops in blood pressure
options.B: To keep from tearing the hospital mattress
options.C: To protect the skin from friction and tearing
options.D: To avoid setting off the nurse call bell

explanation: Well done! Dragging causes friction and shear forces that damage delicate skin layers and tiny blood vessels underneath. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: How do pillows and wedges help when positioning a patient?

options.A: By taking pressure off bony body parts
options.B: By keeping the patient awake during the day
options.C: By making the hospital bed much taller
options.D: By soaking up sweat and wound drainage

explanation: Exactly! Pillows bridge gaps and lift heavy body parts away from vulnerable bony areas to keep the skin safe. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient lies flat on their back during a tummy examination. What position are they in?
explanation: Spot on! Lying flat on the back with face and torso facing upward is called the supine position. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is the prone position sometimes used for patients with serious breathing trouble?

options.B: It can help improve oxygen flow in the lungs
options.C: It makes eating meals much easier
options.D: It keeps the spine in a straight line

explanation: You're right! Lying on the stomach changes how chest pressure works and helps open up areas of the lungs. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the Sims position most commonly used for?

options.B: Feeding patients who have trouble swallowing

explanation: Great job! The Sims position gives the best access and comfort for lower bowel procedures. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: How does turning a patient onto their side protect their skin?

options.A: It takes body weight off the tailbone and heels
options.B: It helps the skin make natural oils
options.C: It seals skin breaks from the air
options.D: It stops the patient from sweating at night

explanation: Spot on! Shifting weight away from heavy bony areas like the tailbone helps prevent painful pressure sores. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the standard bed angle for Fowler's position?
explanation: You got it! Raising the bed head to 45–60 degrees creates a comfortable balance for rest and daily care. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h5)

question: A patient suddenly struggles to breathe while in bed. What should you do first?

options.A: Turn them onto their left side
options.B: Raise the head of the bed to High Fowler's
options.D: Lay them flat on their stomach

explanation: Well done! Sitting the patient up expands the chest and quickly eases sudden breathing distress. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h5)

question: In the Trendelenburg position, how is the bed tilted?
explanation: Spot on! Trendelenburg tilts the whole bed so the head is lower than the rest of the body. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of the Reverse Trendelenburg position?

options.A: It quickly raises blood pressure in shock
options.B: It reduces acid reflux and helps stomach emptying
options.C: It makes giving enemas much easier
options.D: It prevents foot drop during long bed rest

explanation: You're correct! Gravity helps keep stomach contents down, which is great for patients prone to reflux. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which position requires a patient to place their feet inside stirrups?
explanation: Great work! The lithotomy position uses stirrups to support the legs while the patient lies on their back. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h7)

question: What safety risk goes up when a patient stays in the lithotomy position for too long?

options.B: Nerve damage and poor leg circulation

explanation: Spot on! Long hours in stirrups can press on leg nerves and blood vessels, so nurses monitor this closely. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h7)

question: How often should you turn an immobile patient to prevent bed sores?

options.A: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: You got it! Repositioning every two hours relieves constant pressure and keeps the skin healthy. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h8)

question: Which bone is at high risk for pressure sores when a patient lies on their side?
explanation: Well done! The side-lying position puts direct pressure on the side of the hip, needing extra padding. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h8)

question: Which detail is NOT needed when charting a patient turn?

options.A: The exact time you turned the patient
options.B: The brand name of the mattress
options.C: Skin check findings over pressure points

explanation: Spot on! Mattress brands are equipment details, not clinical nursing notes about the patient's care. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h9)

question: Why is timely charting of patient positions so important in the ward?

options.A: It guarantees the patient goes home early
options.B: It stops doctors from writing notes
options.D: It proves care was given and keeps the team informed

explanation: You're right! Good charting serves as a legal record and shares important care updates with the next shift. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h9)
